system.biography:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Arcanium flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Arcane Herb.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.
You take half damage from Arcane attacks or damage.

Your attacks may deal Physical or Arcane damage. When you deal Arcane damage, the target loses 1 MP though they get to make a Save if this was a light attack. Furthermore, any target ending its turn while rooted by your Consume loses 1 MP.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.
You may Sidestep 5ft.

system.biography: The manticore is a monstrous combination of three different types of animal originally fused together through magic. They possess little intelligence and do little more than feast on anyone unfortunate enough to run into one.

details.appearance: A large creature with the body of a lion, a scorpion like tail and a large pair of wings.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild or in a dungeon.

system.tactics: The manticore will open with Lion's roar. If it managed to slow any targets, it will focus on that target with its crushing maw. If no enemies were affected by the roar or if there's no enemies in range to attack, it will use tail spikes. Afterwards, it wil attack with the tail.
system.runningMonster:
The manticore can be run together with 3 other heroic creatures to make a good challenge.

Gather Parts: 500 units of direhide.

system.description: When making a basic Light or Heavy attack with your maw, you become enhanced against Slowed targets. If it’s a Light attack, you gain Sure Hit. If it’s a Heavy attack, you gain Full Pierce.
When making a basic Light or Heavy Attack, you may attack with either your head or tail. You gain a benefit based on the body part chosen.
When making a basic Light or Heavy attack with your tail, you inflict Daze on dealing damage. If the target is already Dazed, you instead deal 5 (Light) or 10 (Heavy) Full Pierce Poison damage.
All enemies within range must make a Save or become Unbalanced. They also become Slowed until the end of your next turn.

You firee a hail of spikes at a 15x15 ft area, making a Light attack against all enemies within the area. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already Dazed, they instead take 5 poison damage.

system.biography: A creature often confused with the chimera of Northi. Despite a similar appearance, the original minotaur is a cursed creature once locked away in a labyrinth. Its offspring now roam the world, causing destruction wherever they go.

details.appearance: A creature with the body of a man and the head of a bull.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the world.

system.tactics: The minotaur will use all their AP on Goring Charge if not in range of an enemy. Once in range, they will attack normally and use Headbutt when they can.
system.runningMonster: A group of minotaurs provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Its stats are fairly high, but its abilities are unimpressive and it mostly just basic attacks.

system.description: Your skull is exceptionally hard. You are immune to Daze and non-magical Stun effects.

You lower your head as you charge and look to crash into either the target or an obstacle barring your path. Any object that is not made of sufficiently thick metal or stone (DM Discretion) is destroyed in the charge. Any creature behind said object is immediately knocked Prone and takes Light damage.

If this attack hits a creature, you will make a Heavy attack on the target. When using more than 2 AP on this movement, you gain an additional 1 focus and 2 power on this attack. On damage if the creature has less toughness than you, they are immediately knocked Prone and Dazed.
On dealing damage with a melee attack, you can follow-up with a headbutt as a Light attack. On damage the target is Unbalanced.
system.requirement: Landing a normal Light or Heavy attack

system.biography: A huge humanoid monster that possess some form of intelligence similar to that of a human child. They are often easily tricked by skilled manipulators who use them for their own goals.

details.appearance: A huge humanoid with a rugged look. An ogre can easily be 10 foot tall.

system.tactics: The ogre will use Smash you and Smash you more whenever it can, attacking the nearest enemy.
system.runningMonster: A group of ogres provides a good challenge for a group of adventurers.

system.description: Upon being reduced to half HP, you go into a tantrum like rage. While in this state, increase your Power by 2. If you are Stunned or Weakened this state will end for the rest of combat.
You make a Heavy attack against the target. If the target has less toughness than the Ogre’s power, they become dazed.
After successfully “Dazing” a target with “SMASH YOU” , you make an additional Heavy Attack on the target and on unguarded hit the target is knocked Prone.

system.biography:
Summon cost: 4 AP, 4 Mana

10x10ft size

system.description: This creature has an upkeep of 2 AP and counts as 2 towards your summon limit.
If you make an attack of opportunity, you can make a Heavy attack for 0 RP instead of 1. You gain a +2 bonus to accuracy checks when making attacks of opportunity.
Until the start of your next turn, the target is Challenged by you.
Your next Block action against an enemy Challenged by you costs 0 RP.
You make a Light attack against the target  On damage, the target is moved 5ft away from you if the target is no more than twice your size.

system.biography: Priests are spellcasters that draw their power from the gods. Due to the popularity and strength of Kari, the human goddess, the vast majority of priests in the world are human. However, priests of other races do still exist. Some may follow Kari, while others may follow their own god or goddess.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics:
A priest will want to play close to the frontlines to be in range for Angel’s Embrace. Once the melee’s of each side have engaged on combat, the priest can drop a hallowed ground in such a way that it affects all of their melee allies. Afterwards, they will focus on attacking and will use their remaining mana to cast Cure Touch once an ally (heroic allies only if there is any left) becomes low on HP.

Angel’s Embrace can be used to absorb big hits on allies, though the priest should stop using it unless to prevent a killing blow once their own RP becomes too low.
system.runningMonster:
Priests are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being both a support and healer. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Acolyte’ generic enemy.

Priests can function with Grunt level allies, though their support will not be nearly as effective as when supporting heroic allies. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Priests can use either a channeling weapon or a light melee weapon + shield. Priests can wear anything from no armor, light armor to medium armor. In the stat block above, a light melee weapon + shield and light armor is assumed.

system.description: Your Healing spells do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

You grant the target ally Angel’s Embrace granting a shield against the triggering attack that blocks damage equal to 2 + (2 x Toughness)

This spell does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
You heal the target for 11 + (2 x Power)

You bless the ground in a 10ft radius around yourself. Allies in the blessed ground regain HP equal to their Toughness when they spend an RP. The blessed ground remains set in place, even when you move.

system.biography:
The raiju is often confused for an animal due to its appearance. In reality, its an elemental that serves as the hunting dog for a more powerful elemental creature. It will track and hound an enemy from afar, then move in for the kill once the weather changes.

Storms have an unnaturally high chance of appearing when this creature is around.

details.appearance: A white wolf like creature around which electricity constantly crackles.
details.habitat: Rarely found anywhere in the wild. Only seen by those it is hunting.

system.tactics:
The Raiju's strategy is the same regardless of whether its storming or not. It will start by using Static Field at encounter start.

On its turn, it will use Static Charge to pass through as many enemies as it can, without having to move before using Lightning Charge. The remaining AP will be used on attacking.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of Raiju will provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. During a storm, you'll want to lower the amount if you want to keep the difficulty similar as the same group of Raiju can quickly murder a group of low level adventurers.

If it is hunting one of the party members, you can have the Raiju focus on that party member even at risk to themselves.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hide.

system.description: You take no damage from Lightning damage.
Your Focus, Power and Agility are doubled during a storm.

You turn into a ball of lightning and Sidestep in a straight line to a square within range. You can pass through units while doing so and may make a Light attack against each unit you pass through. This attack deals Lightning damage.

You creater a field of lightning around yourself. Any creature that ends its turn within 5ft of you gains Static X, where X is your power x 2.

The range of the field is increased to 10ft during a storm.

system.biography: Summon cost: 3 AP, 2 Mana.

system.description: This summon has an upkeep of 1 AP per creature and counts as 1 towards your summon limit.

A creature with Rush gets a turn immediately when being summoned, and the summoning range is increased to 60ft.  If summoned in the middle of your turn, then take this creature's turn first, then finish the remainder of your turn.

You may spend 2 or 4 AP on this ability and move as though you had spent that AP on movement. After you finish moving, you may spend half of the AP you used on this ability on light or heavy melee attacks.

system.biography: An artificially made elemental creature that was created by a powerful Yuki Onna. Often is disguised as regular ice, but too slow to take advantage of any surprises.

details.appearance: A small creature made out of ice.
details.habitat: Found in area's with lots of snow and ice.

system.tactics: The Rime Vermin uses Self Icicle Nail to get in range if it can. When in range to attack, it will use Heavy attacks if it can and otherwise will just use Light attacks.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of around 16 rime vermin makes a challenging fight for a group of 4. You can replace 4 of these to replace them with a heroic unit that might benefit from the ice the rime vermin create. 

Gather Parts: Using gather parts nets a Rime Vermin Ball, which functions like an Elemental Mixture Flask (Frost) and is worth 200 Clim.

system.description: You take double damage from Fire damage.
You take half damage from Frost damage.
When killed, the spot you were killed on turns into ice and becomes difficult terrain for other creatures.
You curl up into a spike shape and fly towards an enemy. You sidestep to and make a Light attack against an enemy within range.

system.biography: Rogues are shifty individuals that use trickery and dirty tactics to win battles. They exist in every race and society.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: Rogues aim for the backline, targeting enemy mages or archers. They can slip past the frontlines using Feint and can avoid enemy attacks by using their 0 RP evasive maneuver. If an enemy is at 0 RP, they can move to that enemy and use their Devastating Strike on them.
system.runningMonster:
Rogue are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on skirmishing. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Assassin’ generic enemy.

Rogues can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Rogues prefer light or no armor along with a pair of light weapons, usually daggers.

system.description: You may use Evasive Maneuver for 0 RP instead of its normal cost.
You move 5ft in any direction and do not trigger any Attacks of Opportunity from this movement.
You make a Light attack against the target.
You do not provoke attacks of opportunity from the target.

system.biography: A skeleton warrior summoned by necromancers.

details.appearance: An armored skeleton wielding a greatsword.

system.description: You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.
You regenerate Toughness HP at the start of your turn.
You make a Light (1 AP), Heavy (2 AP) or Precise (2 AP) attack against the enemy.
You make a Heavy attack against the target. Afterwards, you may sidestep up to twice your speed towards the target of the attack.
system.requirement: Can be used when you would make an attack of opportunity.

system.biography: These creatures are created by skilled necromancers and due to their regenerative abilities will often out live their masters. Though they are mindless, their former instructions still linger and they are likely to attack any creatures that approach it.

details.appearance: A large skeletal creature that has 2 pairs of extra arms. It sits low to the floor and uses one of the pairs of arms to support its weight. Despite this, it still towers above the average person. Their frontal arms are sharpened into blades instead of having hands.
details.habitat: Usually found in places a necromancer has been.

system.tactics:
The Skeletal Monstrosity’s battle strategy is simple. It will attack a random target (or the target that did the most damage to it the previous round) and use Skeletal Armblade Barrage. Afterwards, it will use the sweep against the largest group of targets. After those two attacks, it will keep making light and heavy attacks as appropriate.

If there are no enemies in his attack range, which is 10ft, it will use Bone Spike Shot until an enemy is pulled within its range, then continue with the above mentioned strategy.
system.runningMonster:
The Skeletal Monstrosity is a good enemy to face by itself. Against stronger parties, you can add a few normal skeletons to the mix or give the creature additional arms to further boost its action economy.

Token wise, you want to have a bigger token for the main body (10x10ft token) and then 4 5x5ft tokens for each of the arms. The arms should be adjacent to the main body in some way.

system.description: You have 4 arms which can be targeted separately from the main body. For each active arm, you gain 1 AP. Each arm has 40 HP and uses the Dodge and Guard of the main body. They have 1 RP, which regenerates at the start of your turn. Each arm is attached to the main body and moves along with it. They otherwise have a movement speed of 0 and are immune to Knockbacks, Prone and other disabling effects. An AoE attack only does damage to 1 part of your body, either the main body or an arm, which is chosen by the attacker.
Each of your individual parts regenerates Toughness HP at the start of your turn. This continues even after a body part reaches 0 HP until all body parts have been reduced to 0 HP or lower.
Your attacks can attack targets up to 10ft away.
You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.

You fire a spike from your mouth, making a Precise attack against the target. On damage, the target is pulled next to you in the most direct line possible. If the space next to you is blocked by another creature, the target is placed as closest to the original square as possible.

You make a Light attack against the target and any enemies adjacent to it. On damage, they are knocked back 20ft.

If at least 3 arms are still alive, you may repeat this attack against a different target within range.

You make a Light attack against the target. This attack deals Light damage X amount of times, where X is the amount of arms still alive (Max 4). These are considered separate instances of damage, so you don’t add the damage together before subtracting the guard from it.

system.biography: Skeletons are the bones of people long dead that have been reanimated, usually through necromancy but rarely through astra corruption. They are mindless undead, swinging a weapon - often times a bone of themselves - at the closest living creature they see.

details.appearance: A humanoid skeleton.
details.habitat: Usually found in places a necromancer has been.

system.tactics: The skeletons attacks the nearest target.
system.runningMonster: The skeleton is a very weak monster, especially against groups that possess bludgeoning attacks. A large group of skeletons is needed to provide a good challenge for a group of adventurers.

system.description: You take double damage from Bludgeoning weapons.
You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.
When you reach 0 HP, you are revived with 1 HP at the start of your next turn. Any damage dealt to you while you have 0 HP disables this ability.

Just a slime.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Alchemy units.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.

system.biography: Sniper is a title given to all users of ranged weaponry that display some level of skill. They exist in every race and can use a wide variety of ranged weapons.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics:
The sniper’s strategy in combat is to sit still as far away as possible and do damage to the most vulnerable target. What the most vulnerable target is may change during the course of the battle and a sniper can easily adapt to the situation.

They can use Homing Shot when dealing with high dodge characters. If they are engaged in melee combat, they will use Disengaging Shot if they have mana for it. If they don’t, the common strategy is to switch to a melee weapon.
system.runningMonster:
Snipers are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on ranged combat. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Archer’ generic enemy.

Snipers can be run together with several grunt level enemies or in a group together with around 3 similar heroic enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Snipers can use any type of ranged weapon, though pistols, shotguns and sniper rifles are rarely seen. Snipers often wear no or light armor. Most will also carry a melee weapon as a backup weapon.

system.description: If you didn’t move since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1d4 bonus to all accuracy checks.
You make a heavy attack against the target  with a ranged weapon or a thrown weapon.
system.range: Ranged Weapon Range or Thrown Weapon Range

system.description: You make a ranged weapon Heavy attack against an enemy in range that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Afterwards, you may sidestep up to your speed.
You may make a heavy attack against the target  with a ranged weapon or a thrown weapon.  You do not add your focus to the accuracy roll.
system.range: Ranged Weapon Range or Thrown Weapon Range

system.biography: Tacticians are found in virtually every society and can be of any race. Oftentimes, but not always, they are leaders such as a captain, general or something simpler like a bandit chief. They lead their troops to victory not always through charisma, but through tactics.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: The tactician relies mostly on their troops to do the damage. Their job is to apply Focus Fire to the target most vulnerable or which is reachable by the most of their troops. They can use reposition to cut off escapes or make their allies easily reach the backline. They will always use Stratagem: Lightning at the start of the encounter.
system.runningMonster:
Tacticians are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on tactics and leadership. They can easily be used for any race or situation that requires it.

A tactician is worthless without a good number of grunt level allies. They can pair well with both melee attackers with Stratagem: Lightning and Reposition, but also ranged attackers due to easier Focus Fire usage.

With Battle Tactics, you are free to play the enemies as smartly as you can, roleplaying it as the tactician giving precise orders. Tacticians can use a wide variety of weapons and armor depending on the race or society they are from. Ranged weapons are generally preferable, as a tactician going down may lead to an instant loss.

official.notableSkills: Knowledge History+11, Perception+10, Negotiation+11, Intimidation+11, Deception+10

system.description: All Grunt level allies under your command gain a +1 bonus to their Focus and Agility.
All Grunt level allies under your command  will fight more intelligently, being more likely to target enemies that are weak or out of position

When your HP reaches 0 or lower, all Grunt level allies under your command experience Morale Failure. Unless there is another Heroic level ally on the battlefield, all Grunt level allies will attempt to flee the battlefield, potentially instantly ending the encounter.

You mark an enemy as the target until the start of your next turn. All Grunt level allies under your command must attack that target if they are able to do so without moving. They gain a +1 Power bonus to attacks against this target.
You choose a Grunt level willing ally within range. That ally may sidestep up to twice their movement speed.
All allied units (including yourself) gain +1 to initiative and may immediately move up to their speed.
system.range: All allies in sight, including yourself.

system.biography: Tanks are front liners who go in first and absorb the hits for their allies. Existing in every culture and of any race, they are usually heavily armored with shields.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: The tank’s strategy is to move up to take space, then provoke the closest melee enemy he can.
system.runningMonster:
Tanks are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on being a tanky frontline. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Defender’ generic enemy.

Tank can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

The above stat block assumes they are using Medium Armor and a Shield. Any melee weapon can work for a tank

system.description: If you make an attack of opportunity, you can make a Heavy attack for 0 RP instead of 1. You gain a +2 bonus to accuracy checks when making attacks of opportunity.
Until the start of your next turn, the target is Challenged by you.

system.biography:
Trolls descend from what were once regular humans that mutated into these hideous creatures. 

In a way, they are similar to what hobgoblins are to normal goblins. Perhaps because of this, they are often found in the company of them.

details.appearance: A large ugly humanoid.

system.tactics: The troll simply attacks the nearest target. It should only react to Heavy attacks.
system.runningMonster: A group of trolls provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Its stats are fairly high, but its abilities are unimpressive and it mostly just basic attacks.

system.description: You take double damage from Fire damage.
If you were not hit with a Heavy Attack during the last turn, heal for 30 HP.
Placeholder ability so site doesn't break

system.biography: Unstable Efreets are split off parts of a normal Efreet. Their very existence is a fleeting thing with them being able to exist for little more than day before their flames going out and them vanishing into nothingness.

details.appearance: A creature of pure fire and flame that appears roughly in a humanoid shape.

system.tactics: Unstable Efreet’s strategy is very simple. They will run towards the nearest enemy and attack them until they die and explode.
system.runningMonster: For the most effective use, Unstable Efreets should not start too far away from the players, otherwise they might cause a chain reaction of explosions before they get in range. Be careful when putting these against a Pyromancer. Pyromancers can trivialize this encounter by tagging them with fire spells, but if they do it while the Unstable Efreets are too close, then they could cause a chain reaction that leads to a constant barrage of explosions on the players.

system.description: When your HP is lowered to 0, you will immediately use Explode Self as a reaction. After that, you immediately die.
When you take fire damage, you will start to explode. At the end of your next turn, your HP will be set to 0 and you will use Explode Self.
You take half damage from all fire damage and your attacks deal fire damage.
You make a Precise attack that deals fire damage against all creatures within range. This attack deals Heavy damage instead of its normal damage.

system.biography: Warriors are combatants that specialize in melee combat. They exist in every race and civilization and can use a wide variety of weapons and armor.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.

system.tactics: Warriors use Charge to engage the frontline in combat and hit the most vulnerable target there. If engaged with two or more enemies, they will use Cleaving Strike. Else, they will use Skullsplitter if the target is wearing at least medium armor.
system.runningMonster:
Warriors are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being a hardhitting melee. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Brute’ generic enemy.

Warriors can function with Grunt level allies, but they will want some tank type allies to not get focused down as hard. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Warriors generally use heavy melee weapons. They can use no armor, light armor or medium armor depending on the race. The stat block above assumes light armor and a heavy melee weapon. Some might carry a ranged weapon as backup.

system.description: You are immune to Knockbacks and cannot be knocked prone.

You may spend 2 or 4 AP on this ability and move as though you had spent that AP on movement. After you finish moving, you may spend half of the AP you used on this ability on light or heavy melee attacks.
You make a Heavy attack against two different targets in range.
You make a Heavy attack against the target.

system.biography:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Vivinthal flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Water Herb.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.

You take half damage from Fire and Water attacks or damage, but you take 50% more from Lightning type attacks and damage. You are immune to Soaked, can swim at twice your speed and breathe underwater.
Your attacks may deal Water or Physical damage. When you deal Water damage, you inflict Soaked X where X is your Power.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.
You heal the target for 9 + Power x 3 HP. You may use either AP or RP for this ability.

system.biography: To do.

details.appearance: A heavily armored man or woman riding an armored mount.

system.tactics: Westrian Heavy Paladins aim to charge towards the enemy backline with mounted charge, aiming to move through as many enemies as possible to get there. Once they are in melee range, they will use Divine Smite on each of their turns while their mana lasts. As Divine Shield is free, they will use it at the start of each turn.
system.runningMonster:
A small group of around 4 heavy paladins would make a challenging encounter for a group of players. As they are mounted enemies, they benefit from an open fighting field and are unsuitable for indoor fights.

Heavy Paladins are intelligent creatures and veteran fighters. Don't be afraid to play them intelligently. If a paladin can hit a demon in their divine release state with their divine smite, they should always do so unless it would cause them to provoke too many attacks.

system.description: You have a mount that has 25 HP and uses your defensive stats in combat. It follows the normal horse mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft.

You may move up to twice your movement in a straight line towards a target further than 20ft away and gain Trample after moving at least 20ft. While under the effects of trample, you don't provoke attacks of opportunity by moving and you can move into enemies that are at least one size smaller than your mount. An enemy may spend 1 RP to move out of the way to an empty spot within 5ft of them.

If they don’t move out of the way, you make a Sure Hit Light attack against them. On damage, you knock them prone into the square you came from and keep moving, occupying the square they were in. Otherwise your movement action ends.

When you reach the target you make a Heavy attack against them
You make a Heavy attack that deals Holy damage against the target. Against Demons in their Divine Release state, this attack gains Full Pierce and does maximum damage instead of rolling.
You automatically use the Block action against the next attack targeting you.

system.biography: When a creature is slain by a Wraith, there's a high chance a Wight will be born from its corpse. Wights are automatically subservient to the Wraith that killed them and must stay within a mile radius of it or disappear entirely.

details.appearance: A translucent white creature with a vaguely humanoid shape.
details.habitat: Appears around places where a Wraith is.

system.tactics: The wight will attacks the closest target. It can choose between Spectral Touch or Draining Touch + a light attack, both are valid options.
system.runningMonster:
Wights are very strong against physical attackers. Even a small group of wights can be annoying to fight when you don't have any non-physical damage. Consider the party's abilities very carefully when choosing how many wights to put in.

You can choose to have Wights use their RP immediately, which opens them up for physical attackers, or have them save their RP so they can always react to the physical attackers. The first option will make the fight more manageable for the party members who don't have magical damage options.

system.description: You do not spend your RP when reacting against a physical attack made with a non-magical weapon. A weapon that is enchanted counts as magical.
You may move through solid objects and enemies with no penalty.

You touch the target and attempt to steal its strength, making a Light attack against the target. On damage, you gain a bonus to your Power for your next attack this turn equal to the target's Power. The target's Power becomes 0 until after its next attack.
You attempt to attack the soul of the target with a touch, making a Heavy attack against the target.

Just a slime.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Sylphsteel flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Wind Herb.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.
You take half damage from Wind attacks or damage and gain +2 Evasion against ranged attacks.
Your attacks may deal Physical or Wind damage. You may Sidestep 5ft after every attack.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.
You may Sidestep 5ft.

system.biography: A normal wolf. Occasionally kept as pet.

details.appearance: A normal wolf

system.tactics: The wolves will try to swarm a target, though they won't take attacks of opportunity to do so. They will keep using topple prey until the target is prone, then the other wolves will use go for the throat.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of wolves will make a good challenge for a group of adventurers, ideally led by an Alpha Wolf. All wolves move at the same time to let them gain a huge bonus to their hit rolls before attacking.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hide.

system.description: For each other Wolf adjacent to the target, a Wolf gets a +2 bonus to accuracy rolls on attacks against that target.
When you and other wolves move on your initiative, all of you move before making any attacks.
You make a Heavy Attack against the target.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target falls Prone.

system.biography: A vengeful spirit that died in the darkness while it was still alive. Brought back to life through a necromancer or through astra corruption, they attack any living creature that they can see. They are weak to bright lights and will never willingly go into the sunlight.

details.appearance: A translucent dark creature with a vaguely humanoid shape.
details.habitat: Found only in permanently dark places.

system.tactics:
The Wraith will avoid bright light the best it can, only going in if it has no other choice. It may use Darkness in this case to negate the effects of it if possible.

If it doesn't need to avoid bright light, it will use Darkness after spending 3 AP, then immediately follow up with Darkness Shade to hide.

For attacks, it will use the Spectral Touch and Draining Touch. Like other incorporeal enemies, it can freely react to any physical attacks without burning RP.
system.runningMonster:
A group of wraith's can provide a good challenge to a high spirit core party. At this point, most people should have a way of dealing non-physical weapon. The wraith's stats are a bit higher than the other incorporeal enemies, so be careful because some members of the party may have 0 chance of hitting it even with that.

Having a source of bright light also helps the players. A torch alone wouldn't qualify, but a northi lantern or a paladin's holy weapon might.

system.description: A non-heroic creature reduced to 0 HP by you immediately rises as a Wight after 24 hours have passed.
You do not spend your RP when reacting against a physical attack made with a non-magical weapon. A weapon that is enchanted counts as magical.
If you are in an area with a bright light, become Weakened.
You may move through solid objects and enemies with no penalty.

You conjure an area of pure darkness in a 30x30 ft area around it, centered on yourself. In the darkness, non-magical light ceases to function.

 

The darkness lasts until your next turn.

If you are in a dark area, you attempt to Hide without using AP. When hiding in darkness, you may stay hidden if you are in direct Line of Sight of others. Leaving the dark area or having any source of light illuminate the area will immediately reveal you.

You touch the target and attempt to steal its strength, making a Light attack against the target. On damage, you gain a bonus to your Power for your next attack this turn equal to the target's Power. The target's Power becomes 0 until after its next attack.
You attempt to attack the soul of the target with a touch, making a Heavy attack against the target.

system.biography: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. Though they spent most of their time sleeping in their caves, they are hostile to all living creatures and view them are little more than prey. Wyrms are older, more intelligent and more dangerous than their Drake and Wyrmling counterparts.

details.appearance: A large scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
details.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.

system.tactics:
The firewyrm will rain fire from the sky until it is forced down to the ground or it runs out of mana. Even when out of mana, it may still choose to do fly-by attacks instead of staying on the ground.

While in the sky, it can use both Fireball and Flame Breath at the largest group of enemies. On the ground, it will use tail swipe as the final action of each round and may still use flame breath if it has mana left.

At the encounter start, it will always use Terrifying Roar.
system.runningMonster:
The firewyrm is a solo monster that is a serious threat to any party without aeromancers. In a space where their flight is limited, they can be less threatening. As they are intelligent creatures, a firewyrm may retreat if the battle starts going badly for it.

The firewyrm is bigger than a drake, but the token size is still the same.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of dragonscale.

system.description: When you inflict Burning on a target that is already suffering from Burning, they immediately take Fire damage equal to the existing Burning value.
You take no damage from Fire damage.

You can fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so. While flying, you may make any of your attacks (spending AP as normal) during your movement and continue to move afterwards.
You gain +1 Guard, and a further +2 Guard when taking the Block action (Already added to stats).
You breathe fire in a 30ft cone, making a Light attack against all creatures in it. On damage, a target becomes Burning X, where X is your Power x 3.
You make a Light attack against every creature in a 15x15 ft square. On damage, a target becomes Burning X, where X is your Power x 3.
You spin around your axis and attack every creature within 10ft of you with a Light attack. On damage, a target is pushed back 15ft.
All creatures that can hear the roar of the firewyrm must make a save or become Shaken. This effect lasts until the end of combat, or until the target uses 3 AP to remove the effect from themselves.

system.biography: Mindless corpses resurrected through necromancy or astra corruption.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature with decaying skin.
details.habitat: Found in places with corpses or near necromancers.

system.tactics: Zombies move towards the near enemy. If the target is not already grabbed (by any zombie) and they can make a Heavy attack, they make a Heavy attack. Otherwise if they are not already grabbing an enemy, they will do so.
system.runningMonster: A large group of zombies is a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Zombies are weak to holy damage, so you will want to add more of them to keep the challenge the same when the players have classes like a paladin or priest with them. Zombies are slow, but relatively tanky for a grunt enemy. Against parties that are less likely to exploit this weakness or if fighting in a place where its impossible to do, you may want to use slightly less zombies.

system.description: You take double damage from Holy damage.
You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.

You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, you and the target are both Rooted.

The target may spend 1 AP to break free, after which the target and you are both no longer rooted. If the target is grabbed by multiple enemies through this ability, spending the 1 AP will free it from all grabs.
